ip_top_stories.title: Microsoft exec called AI scraping 'the largest theft of labor in human history,' new unredacted filings reveal
ip_top_stories.summary: Newly unsealed court filings in the New York Times v. OpenAI/Microsoft lawsuit reveal that a Microsoft executive internally described AI training on copyrighted content as 'the largest theft of labor in human history.' The documents also show OpenAI and Microsoft staff acknowledged AI posed an 'existential threat' to news publishers. News outlets are arguing these admissions directly undermine the defendants' fair use copyright defence.

ip_top_stories.title: OpenAI, Microsoft executives' quotes on AI training threaten copyright defense, news outlets argue
ip_top_stories.summary: News organisations suing OpenAI and Microsoft are citing internal executive statements — including acknowledgements of an 'existential threat' to publishers and descriptions of AI training as mass theft — as evidence against the companies' fair use defence. The filings were unsealed as part of the ongoing New York Times copyright litigation. Publishers Weekly covers the implications for the broader copyright case.

ip_top_stories.title: Coders lose appeal in copyright fight against AI tools
ip_top_stories.summary: A US appeals court has ruled against software developers who brought a copyright infringement case over the use of their code to train AI coding tools, including GitHub Copilot. The decision represents a significant win for OpenAI and Microsoft and narrows the legal avenues available to plaintiffs in AI training copyright disputes.

ip_top_stories.title: Opt-out AI training plan could weaken Australian copyright protections
ip_top_stories.summary: A proposed Australian government policy that would allow AI companies to train on copyrighted content unless rights holders actively opt out has drawn sharp criticism from authors and publishers. Critics argue the plan effectively reverses the existing copyright framework and could expose Australian creators' work to large-scale AI scraping without meaningful consent or compensation.

ip_top_stories.title: New California law mandates AI performer disclosure in ads
ip_top_stories.summary: California has enacted legislation requiring advertisers to disclose when AI-generated likenesses or voices are used in place of human performers. The law adds a new layer of regulation to the use of AI-generated content in commercial contexts, with implications for both intellectual property and performer rights.

ip_further_links.title: OpenAI an 'existential' threat to publishers, unsealed US litigation statements say
ip_further_links.summary: Unsealed statements from the NYT v. OpenAI litigation show company insiders acknowledged the existential risk AI posed to the news publishing industry.

ip_further_links.title: OpenAI, Microsoft fend off part of software developer lawsuit over AI training
ip_further_links.summary: A US court partially dismissed claims by software developers against OpenAI and Microsoft over AI training on code, though some claims were allowed to proceed.

ip_further_links.title: Richard Flanagan on AI policy: Albanese isn't just betraying authors like me. He's selling out Australia to AI colonists
ip_further_links.summary: Australian novelist Richard Flanagan argues that the Albanese government's proposed opt-out AI copyright framework betrays creators and cedes Australian cultural output to foreign AI companies.

ip_further_links.title: Government ditches controversial AI plan in media showdown
ip_further_links.summary: The Australian government has abandoned a controversial AI copyright proposal following intense pushback from media organisations and creators.

ip_further_links.title: Everything Australians put online could be scraped for AI under proposed new rules. How will you be affected?
ip_further_links.summary: An explainer on how Australia's proposed opt-out AI training rules could affect individual creators, journalists, and publishers whose online content may be freely scraped.

ip_further_links.title: Caution on copyright changes as Claude comes to town
ip_further_links.summary: Commentary on growing Australian caution around proposed copyright changes coinciding with Anthropic's expanding presence in the country.

ip_further_links.title: Microsoft, OpenAI's Narrow Copyright Win Avoids Damages Threat
ip_further_links.summary: Analysis of the partial dismissal in the software developer copyright case, noting that while OpenAI and Microsoft secured a narrow win, significant legal exposure remains.

ip_further_links.title: AI vs Journalism: The Battle for Fair Use
ip_further_links.summary: An overview of the ongoing legal and ethical battle between AI developers and news publishers over fair use doctrine in the context of AI training on journalistic content.

ip_further_links.title: Simone Blackadder gives her two cents on the AI-copyright debate
ip_further_links.summary: Commentary from an Australian creator perspective on the national debate over AI training rights and copyright protections for authors.

ip_further_links.title: Liability, regulation, and AI's new false dichotomy
ip_further_links.summary: Analysis arguing that framing AI governance as a choice between liability and regulation presents a false dichotomy that obscures more nuanced policy options.
